description: We are a six-member interdisciplinary team passionate about AI, software engineering, data science, and space research. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we are building an AI-powered platform to explore microgravity combustion experiments and transform scientific findings into accessible, evidence-backed fire safety insights. Our team combines full-stack development, AI/ML, data engineering, scientific research, UI/UX design, and testing. We aim to turn NASA's research into meaningful innovation.
summary:
FlameLens AI is an AI-powered research support platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 – Flame in Freefall. It addresses the challenges of understanding combustion behaviour in microgravity and making better-informed use of limited experimental opportunities.

The platform brings together four capabilities: a 3D Combustion Laboratory to explore different fuels, atmospheric conditions and gravity environments; an Evidence Explorer to access curated historical combustion research with traceable provenance; a Design Optimizer that uses Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to estimate burning rates and predictive uncertainty, alongside Bayesian Expected Information Gain (EIG) to prioritize potentially informative experimental conditions; and a Comparison Studio to examine experimental conditions, outcomes and data quality across studies.

By connecting historical evidence, scientific visualization and uncertainty-aware experimental planning, FlameLens AI aims to help researchers explore combustion phenomena and identify promising experiments for further investigation. It is a research-support prototype designed to complement scientific expertise and physical experimentation, not replace them.
details:
Project Overview and Functionality

FlameLens AI is an integrated research support platform designed to help researchers explore microgravity combustion, investigate historical experimental evidence and prioritize potentially informative future experiments.

The platform consists of four interconnected modules:

1. 3D Combustion Laboratory: Provides an interactive environment where researchers can explore combustion scenarios by adjusting fuel, pressure, oxygen concentration, initial droplet diameter and gravity conditions. It uses physics-informed visualization, an analytical droplet burning model and empirical predictions where supported.

2. Evidence Explorer: Organizes curated combustion research records from sources including NASA's Public Science and Information (PSI) resources and NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS). It helps researchers discover historical investigations and trace information to its source.

3. Design Optimizer: Uses fuel-specific Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) models to estimate burning rates and predictive uncertainty. Bayesian Expected Information Gain (EIG) is then used to prioritize candidate experimental conditions according to their estimated information value. This helps researchers identify promising experiments to investigate when physical testing opportunities are limited.

4. Comparison Studio: Enables researchers to compare experimental conditions, reported outcomes, missing information and data quality across different studies, while highlighting methodological differences.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FlameLens AI connects fragmented research evidence, interactive scientific visualization and machine-learning-assisted experimental planning in one platform.

Its intended benefits include:

  • Making historical combustion research easier to discover and investigate.
  • Helping researchers explore different combustion conditions and gravity environments.
  • Providing predictive estimates alongside uncertainty information.
  • Supporting the prioritization of potentially informative experiments.
  • Making comparisons between experimental studies more transparent.
  • Encouraging evidence-based decisions when experimental resources are limited.

The long-term vision is to support more informed microgravity combustion research and help researchers make better use of available experimental opportunities.

Technologies and Tools Used

Frontend and Visualization:

  • JavaScript
  • HTML5 and CSS3
  • Vite
  • Three.js
  • WebGL

Backend and Machine Learning:

  • Python
  • Gaussian Process Regression
  • Scikit-learn
  • NumPy and scientific data-processing tools
  • Bayesian experimental design and active-learning methods

Data and Research Sources:

  • NASA PSI-69 FLEX experimental dataset
  • NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS)
  • NASA Task Book and other curated combustion research records

Development and Testing:

  • Visual Studio Code
  • GitHub
  • Vercel
  • Selenium and automated testing tools

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of FlameLens AI is the integration of multiple research capabilities into one connected workflow.

Rather than functioning as only a visualization tool or a conventional machine-learning predictor, it connects historical experimental evidence to interactive combustion exploration and uncertainty-aware experimental planning.

A particularly important innovation is the connection between GPR predictions and EIG-based candidate prioritization. This allows researchers to consider not only what a model predicts, but also where additional experimental observations may provide useful information.

The platform also emphasizes scientific transparency by distinguishing historical measurements, model predictions, uncertainty estimates and hypothetical experimental conditions.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered:

  • Scientific accuracy and traceability of historical evidence.
  • Differences between Earth-gravity and microgravity combustion.
  • Limited experimental opportunities and research resources.
  • Model uncertainty and the limitations of available datasets.
  • Experimental feasibility and hardware constraints.
  • Comparability of measurements from different investigations.
  • Performance, usability and accessibility of the platform.
  • The importance of distinguishing conceptual visualizations from experimentally validated physical simulations.

FlameLens AI is a research-support prototype. Its visualizations and predictions do not replace CFD, physical experiments or expert scientific validation, and it is not endorsed or validated by NASA.

Our ultimate goal is to help researchers move from understanding existing combustion evidence to making more informed decisions about what to investigate next.
